To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
non-verbal, body, emotional and social aspects of interaction are crucial for art and entertainment applications.

(1) active listening to music can be enhanced by means of novel interactive technologies that support non-verbal, social, emotional and full-body interaction; (2) novel paradigms for active music listening can be developed and evaluated in the context of novel interactive technologies, such as those based on the Kinect sensor, and that (3) novel technologies can be used in the development of novel paradigms and applications for active music listening.

non-verbal, body-based interaction can be used in multimedia systems to support active music listening, that the use of body-based interaction can enhance social interaction and communication, and that this type of interaction can be used for a variety of different purposes, from artistic and creative to social and educational.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of interactive systems that enable people to actively engage in social music listening experience by means of full body interaction.
the development of new paradigms and systems for nonverbal full-body emotional and social interaction with music.
novel paradigms for social interaction in the context of active music listening, based on non-verbial full-body interaction and multimodal interfaces.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, the research presented in this paper has been able to provide an innovative approach to music listening experience.
non-verbal, emotional and social interactive systems are a new and promising area in HCI and in multimedia.
non-verbal full-body interaction with multimedia content can provide a new way to experience art, entertainment, and music.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are developing a new generation of interactive systems for music listening that are able to dynamically generate expressive music and audiovisual content in a social context.
the research on HCI and multimedia is a very promising area for developing novel paradigms and systems for art and for entertainment, based on the use of nonverbal, full-body and social interaction.
we are working on novel paradigmas of social active music and sound listening experience.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the design of new HCI paradigms for active music listening should be driven by a careful consideration of the emotional, social and expressive dimensions of the experience, and of the role of full-body interaction.
active music listening is a novel paradigm for music listening, and can be used as a basis for novel interactive applications and systems.
non-verbal, emotional and social aspects of human interaction with technology are important and should not be ignored.
